characteristic_extramedullary_sites: skin (cutaneous mastocytosis/urticaria pigmentosa, especially in indolent forms)
lymph nodes (more common in advanced/aggressive forms)

biomarkers.name: KIT D816V
biomarkers.clinical_use: Diagnostic major molecular driver in most adult SM. Predictive because KIT D816V confers resistance to imatinib (mutation impairs binding). Avapritinib shows high activity in advanced SM; midostaurin also has activity.

biomarkers.name: Serum tryptase
biomarkers.prevalence: >20 ng/mL is a WHO/ICC minor criterion (unless explained by an associated myeloid neoplasm or hereditary alpha-tryptasemia)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Diagnostic; disease burden/response monitoring; hereditary alpha-tryptasemia is an important confounder/differential

biomarkers.name: KIT non-D816V mutations
biomarkers.clinical_use: Imatinib may be effective in selected cases with imatinib-sensitive KIT mutations or wild-type KIT (e.g., K509I, F522C)

biomarkers.name: Multilineage KIT D816V
biomarkers.prevalence: Common in advanced SM and SM-AHN
biomarkers.clinical_use: Detection in non-mast-cell lineages supports multilineage involvement and is associated with more advanced disease biology and worse prognosis

biomarkers.name: SRSF2, ASXL1, RUNX1 (S/A/R mutations)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Adverse prognostic mutations; incorporated into mutation-adjusted prognostic models such as MARS

biomarkers.name: IPSM / MARS score
biomarkers.clinical_use: Risk stratification in SM; IPSM is used across non-advanced and advanced SM contexts, whereas MARS is specifically for advanced SM

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Multifocal dense infiltrates of spindle-shaped/atypical mast cells (≥15 mast cells in aggregates) in bone marrow and/or other extracutaneous organs; mast cells are tryptase+, CD117+, and typically aberrantly CD25+ with or without CD2 and/or CD30 expression
variants: indolent SM (ISM — most common; often cutaneous involvement, minimal organ dysfunction)
histomorphological_subtype.grading: WHO/ICC categories span ISM, SSM, ASM, SM-AHN, and MCL

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Mast cell mediator release (histamine, tryptase, prostaglandins, leukotrienes and other mediators) drives systemic symptoms — flushing, urticaria, anaphylaxis, diarrhoea, hypotension
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Multifocal marrow mast cell aggregates with spindled morphology; bone remodeling abnormalities including osteopenia/osteoporosis or osteosclerosis can occur

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Haematopoietic stem/progenitor cell or mast cell precursor acquiring KIT D816V in many cases, particularly in advanced/multilineage disease
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Multifocal dense infiltrates of spindle-shaped mast cells with atypical morphology; tryptase+, CD117+, aberrant CD25+ with or without CD2 and/or CD30 expression (aberrant expression distinguishes clonal from reactive mast cells)
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: KIT D816V drives constitutive KIT activation independent of SCF ligand. Disease severity spectrum (ISM → SSM → ASM → SM-AHN → MCL) reflects clonal evolution, and additional mutations such as SRSF2, ASXL1, and RUNX1 are characteristic of advanced SM
